parPrice.question: How is a share company's initial (par) price determined?
parPrice.answer: There are no par prices. The initial price is set by the player who purchases the President's certificate, choosing a value selected from a range of predefined prices. All further share dealing is done at the current market price.

maxRevenue.question: Must the maximum possible revenue be claimed?
maxRevenue.answer: Yes, but a lower revenue may be claimed if the president chooses to run via a mine. In this case the run must be the maximum possible including the mine.

forcedTrainAfford.question: When a company is forced to buy a train and cannot buy one with its own means, what train may it then buy?
forcedTrainAfford.answer: Any available train from the bank or bank pool, or from another company with the same president for at least 1.

miscellaneous.question: Miscellaneous
miscellaneous.answer: The game contains obligations , which can be purchased and come with a non-active 10% share of one of the public companies. The holder of an obligation has the option to purchase the president's certificate of the corresponding public company if someone else declares they wish to buy it. When the two cities of the obligation are connected the non-active share becomes a normal share. When a player wons 60% of a company, buying more shares requires that an additional 20% of the price be paid to the bank.
